summary: Ko Kret is a car-free Chao Phraya island in Nonthaburi, known for Mon heritage, pottery, temples and local snacks. It makes a good half- or full-day outing from Bangkok, especially on a weekend when the market is busiest.
whyGo: See the Mon community’s pottery traditions and the island’s distinctive riverside temples, including Wat Poramai Yikawat and its leaning stupa.
Walk or cycle between the pottery area, temple compounds, food stalls and small riverside cafés.
Try local sweets and savory dishes such as khao chae and food made with local kratium (water mimosa) shoots.
bestFor: Travelers interested in local culture, craft, temples and low-key food stops.
A weekend day trip that feels different from central Bangkok without an overnight stay.
skipIf: You need smooth, step-free routes throughout or cannot manage a small ferry and uneven pedestrian lanes.
You want a busy market on a weekday; shops and stalls are more limited then.
duration: Allow 5–7 hours including the Bangkok-to-Pak Kret transfer, ferry, island visit and return. A focused visit to the central market and nearby temples can take about 3–4 hours on the island.
cost: No island admission fee is listed by the Thai tourism directory. TAT reports the Wat Sanam Nuea–Ko Kret ferry at ฿10 per person on weekdays and ฿5 on weekends/public holidays (its article says fares are paid to the boat operator). TAT lists pottery-making at Pa Tum’s workshop at ฿100 per person. Budget separately for food, any bicycle rental and Bangkok transport; confirm prices on arrival.
hours: TAT says the public crossing serves 06:00–19:00. The island welcomes visitors daily, but many shops are open only in part on weekdays; the market is fullest on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. Individual temples, workshops and businesses may keep different hours.
bestTime: Choose a weekend or public holiday for the market, arrive in the morning to avoid the midday heat and allow time for the ferry queue. A weekday visit is quieter but has fewer open shops. December is generally a more comfortable season for walking than the hot season, though shade is limited on exposed paths.
gettingThere: From Bangkok, travel to Wat Sanam Nuea in Pak Kret by taxi/ride-hail, or take public transport toward Pak Kret and a local motorcycle taxi to the pier. Cross to Ko Kret at Wat Poramai Yikawat/Wat Sao Thong Thong; verify which landing is operating when you arrive. The Chao Phraya Express Boat’s current schedule (from 6 October 2026) lists weekday orange-flag Nonthaburi–Rajsingkorn service at ฿19; it does not run on weekends according to that timetable. Nonthaburi pier is not the Ko Kret crossing, so continue overland to Wat Sanam Nuea. The Pink Line to Yaek Pak Kret is another option, then use a local taxi or motorcycle taxi to the pier. Return before the local ferry’s stated 19:00 close.
booking: No booking is indicated for the public Wat Sanam Nuea ferry or general island visit; pay the crossing fare to the operator. Confirm pottery workshop availability directly on arrival. No December 2026 special event or reservation information was found in the official sources reviewed.
accessibility: No authoritative accessibility information was found for the ferry landing, boat boarding or island routes. Expect a small boat crossing, steps or gaps at the pier, and narrow, uneven lanes; this is a practical caution based on the setting, not a published access assessment. Ask the operator before boarding if you use a wheelchair or need step-free access. The island has no cars, which reduces traffic but does not make paths accessible.
practicalTips: Bring cash for the ferry, snacks, workshop fees and small purchases; ask the operator to confirm the fare before boarding.
Use sun protection and carry water. The island route is walkable, but cycling can help cover the roughly 6 km perimeter; check the bicycle and lane conditions before renting.
Dress respectfully for temple visits and check opening locally; TAT describes a route linking Wat Sao Thong Thong, Wat Phai Lom and Wat Poramai Yikawat.
Leave time for the return crossing and your onward trip to Bangkok, especially on a busy weekend.
decemberNotes: December 2026 ferry timetables and fares may change. The Chao Phraya Express Boat page currently specifies a schedule from 6 October 2026, but that service only helps reach Nonthaburi on weekdays; it does not replace the Pak Kret island ferry. Recheck both services shortly before travel. No dated December 2026 event was confirmed.
uncertainties: The TAT article is dated 2023, so its ferry fares and hours are useful published guidance but should be reconfirmed locally for December 2026.
The official express-boat page lists weekday hours as image/table content that was not readable in the page text; check its current timetable directly before relying on a departure time.
Specific ferry accessibility, workshop hours, bicycle hire rates and individual venue opening times were not confirmed in the official sources reviewed.
